summary: Windows exact-head regression exposed destructive lease ownership being collapsed into a reusable workflow fingerprint and then surfaced additional Windows-only SQLite/resource-lifecycle defects. The bounded repair separated exact-launch ownership, corrected cross-platform durability/resource cleanup and passed the complete exact-head cross-platform acceptance run.
root_cause: A reusable PID/start-token workflow fingerprint was also being used as destructive lease ownership. Windows then correctly exposed related file-handle lifecycle and fsync portability defects that POSIX behavior had tolerated or obscured.
repair: Preserve workflow_fingerprint for liveness compatibility, add launch_fingerprint for exact ownership, use same_launch for acquire/release/takeover ownership, treat same-workflow/different-launch as stale ownership, preserve schema-v1 read compatibility, make durability fsync paths Windows-safe, close SQLite ownership on every failed-open/composition path and close test-owned profiles before temporary-directory deletion.
